title: user-cohort-based-gradual-swap-with-latency-safeguards
author: Lena Park
description:
Context: Production rollout of a new decoder scheduling strategy (short-prefix KV-reshuffle) caused sporadic P95 latency regressions in long-lived sessions during an internal canary. Previous rollout controllers focused on traffic weight and cohort percentages but did not enforce session affinity or provide a sliding-latency gate per cohort.

Motivation: Provide a rollout primitive that can perform a gradual model swap targeted at user cohorts while preserving session affinity and enforcing latency SLO safeguards that can pause or partially roll back the swap automatically if latency degrades beyond configured thresholds. This PR implements a controller and API surface for 'CohortGradualSwap' with the following goals: 1) preserve session affinity for stateful users during swaps so in-flight conversations are not disrupted; 2) allow percentage-based cohort targeting (by user-id hash / cookie) with deterministic assignment; 3) enforce adaptive latency gates per cohort (short-term P95 and longer-term moving-average) and pause/roll back automatically when breached; 4) provide observability hooks and a simulator to validate policy behavior offline.

Design summary:
- New CRD: CohortGradualSwap (fields: cohort_selector, target_model, step_percentages, min_step_duration, latency_gates, session_affinity_ttl, fallback_policy).
- Controller: incremental reconciliation loop that applies swaps by annotating routes and updating ServeGraph with traffic weights. The controller retains session-affinity mappings in a small, sharded in-memory store and persists checkpoints to etcd every step to survive leader churn.
- Latency gates: two-layer gating: P95 window (1m granularity) and an exponential moving average (EMA) over 10m for softer stability. Gate evaluation uses existing metrics stream (prometheus exporter) and can be configured with slack multipliers.
- Automatic rollback: when a gate is breached for a cohort for >2 consecutive evaluation windows, the controller performs a targeted rollback of the cohort to the last known-good model and emits an event.
- Simulator: a new simulator binary (tools/rollout-sim) accepts workload traces and gate configs to run simulated rollouts and outputs expected traffic weights, rollback triggers, and estimated user impact.

Migration and backward compatibility: CohortGradualSwap is opt-in. Existing rollout controllers are unchanged. The controller supports a 'compat' mode to translate simple percentage-only swaps into the new CRD for teams that want to adopt incrementally.

Testing:
- Unit tests cover controller reconcilers, affinity mapping logic, and gate evaluation (pkg/rollout/*_test.go).
- Integration tests exercise the end-to-end swap with a mocked metrics sink and a fake ServeGraph (e2e/rollout_latency_test.go).
- Simulator tests include recorded traces from internal production sampling.

Observability and dashboards:
- Added per-cohort dashboards: per-cohort P50/P95, rollback events, session-affinity hit rate, and step progression.
- Tracing: added tags to swap-related spans for easier correlation.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Feature behind feature-flag (rollout.cohort_swap_v1).
- Start with internal canary (10% of users, labeled 'internal').
- Promote to staged cohorts (10 -> 30 -> 60 -> 100) with min_step_duration default 30m.
- The controller will not advance a step unless all gates are green for the cohort for the min_step_duration.
- Emergency kill switch: admin API to abort/pause all CohortGradualSwap controllers.

Related work: ENG-1423 (latency gating), ENG-1487 (session-affinity preservation).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: affinity store growth with many ephemeral users. Mitigation: TTL-based eviction, bloom-filter precheck, and sharded backing to avoid hot keys.
- Risk: noisy metrics causing spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: dual-gate strategy (fast P95 + EMA) and require consecutive windows before rollback.
